subject: Oceanography
title: Mutualism in the Sea
description: Learn Mutualism in the Sea in one minute.

hook.text: Clownfish live inside stinging anemones that would kill any other fish—both benefit from the deal.

buildup.text: The anemone's stinging tentacles protect the clownfish; the clownfish brings food and cleans parasites.

discovery.text: A mucus coating makes clownfish immune to the sting—a chemical trick that took millions of years to evolve.

twist.text: Coral-zooxanthellae is another mutualism—the algae get shelter while providing the coral with 90% of its energy.

climax.text: Mutualism is everywhere in the ocean—cleaning stations, coral partnerships, even bacteria inside tube worms.

punchline.text: In the ocean, the best survival strategy is cooperation.

quiz.question: How does the clownfish survive anemone stings?
options: A special mucus coating makes it immune
It moves too fast to be stung
